excerpt: Gitea supports creating and managing repositories, browsing commit history and code files, reviewing and merging code submissions, managing collaborators, handling branches, and more.
Gitea Actions supports CI/CD functionality, compatible with GitHub Actions. Users can write workflows in familiar YAML format and reuse a variety of existing Actions plugins.
Code review supports both the Pull Request workflow and AGit workflow. Reviewers can browse code online and provide review comments or feedback.
Extend Gitea's functionality with our API and webhooks, creating custom workflows to match your unique needs.

Gitea supports over 20 different types of public or private software package management, including Cargo, Chef, Composer, Conan, Conda, Container, Helm, Maven, npm, NuGet, Pub, PyPI, RubyGems, Vagrant, and more.

Gitea tracks project requirements, features, and bugs through columns and issues. Issues support features like branches, tags, milestones, assignments, time tracking, due dates, dependencies, and more.
Gitea places a strong emphasis on security, offering features such as user permission management, access control lists, and more to ensure the security of code and data.
Sync seamlessly with tools like Slack, Discord, MS Teams, Lark, and more.
It can be easily deployed on various servers without complex configurations or dependencies.
Universally compatible with diverse operating systems and environments, including Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, and Kubernetes. Compatible with multiple architectures, such as x86 and arm64.

Gitea supports more than 20 different kinds of public or private package management, including: Cargo, Chef, Composer, Conan, Conda, Container, Helm, Maven, NPM, NuGet, Pub, PyPI, RubyGems, Vagrant, etc.
The recommended method is to migrate repositories from Gogs to Gitea.
Provides flexible deployment options, supporting both single server setups and replication configurations.
Offers seamless integration with leading databases, including SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL, TiDB, and MS SQL.
I used Gitea to deploy a Git server for a very small project with just 8 users. It was a lot simpler than setting up a full blown Gitlab instance. It is just one binary to get running and that's it.

devops sysadmin here...gitlab is also so large it requires its own chef deployment...it is also massively less resource hungry than a gitlab installation. im currently throwing 4 cores and 8 gigs of ram at my gitlab install...Large installs of 1000 users or more and you'll begin to see why gitlab might not be the best choice.

I've been using Gitea, previously using Gogs, for a team of 45 and have had a very pleasant experience. Getting it up and running with docker was smooth and it works easily with Certbot...it does suffer from a lack of good documentation.

Gitea still got support for OAuth2 which have been simply dropped by Gogs...Gitea still got more really useful features compared to Gogs. But Gitea will always focus on Git hosting and won't bundle with CI, Chat and all that stuff what Gitlab does.
Gitea is awesome. I have been using it for few months and it doesn't need a lot of RAM.
So this is a GitHub alternative … whose source is hosted in GitHub? Instills so much confidence.
I am using Gitea + Drone for several years now and couldn't be happier. Stable, fast and it justs works without consuming a shitload of RAM.
been using it for 4+ years, no complains and it keeps getting better. each upgrade is super simple: just stop the service, replace that one single binary, and start the service.

I'll go against the grain and say, Gitea is good but could use a lot of improvement...there are issues with migrations (up but no down), nonstandard web framework (go-macaron), and far too much logic implemented in go templates...Gitea isn't a great Go codebase.

Gitea is very easy to use, but I find the Activity feature is a little slow...I found the page loading was so slow, nearly 90s...I guess Gitea uses git command to traverse all the logs for the period every time.
For a certain definition of 'painless'. It's fine for a one man show or a small company. Once you get bigger, you start hitting the various issues quite often, and wish for github again.
I sorely lack subscriptions/watches managment in Gitea...There is also no session managment accessible from user side :(

I recently moved over from self-hosting GitLab to instead having Gitea, Nexus and Drone, because the burden of keeping GitLab up to date was cumbersome...Gitea is immeasurably more performant when compared to GitLab, especially when the available hardware resources are limited.
I've been happy with Gitea. It's very fast, and upgrades cannot be simpler. Just download the new binary and start it. The migrations run automatically.
Last time I tried Gitea, it was surprisingly difficult to migrate existing git repos. I hope they made it easier.

One of my previous companies use their self-hosted Gitea...they don't have a dedicated DevOps person, so we actually have to spend extra maintenance on it...it is much easier to just store our source code in one of the SaaS option like Github/GitLab/Bitbucket for our auditors.
I'm grateful for Gitea. It performs well even on slow computers (fitlet2 equipped with an Atom x7-E3950 and 16GB of Ram in my case). Gitlab, on the other hand, doesn't.
There were many positive changes, but what the fuck happens with all the breakages? Reserving usernames and such.
Does Gitea still not have a good mechanism for backup and restore? I wanted to move away from Gogs but this is a show stopper for me.
